data.name: HelpGrid
data.value: The grid: 100 m squares, lettered across (no I or O), numbered down. Say the letter, the number, then where in the square as on a number pad, 7 top left to 3 bottom right: D5-8 is the top middle of D5. YOU, top left, is your square, POINTER the one under the mouse; teammates read theirs off the same grid in their Shturmap.
data.comment: Help: paragraph about the squad grid on the map and how a reference is read and said. D5-8 stays as it is in every language. "As on a number pad": a computer keyboard's number pad (7 8 9 on its top row), not a phone's. YOU and POINTER are the labels at the map's top left (MapGridYou, MapGridPointer): write them as those texts are. Keep the space at the end: the SHOW ME link (HelpShowMe) follows on the same line.

data.name: HelpNotes
data.value: A kept quest card ends in NOTES: your own words on the quest, each with the time you wrote it; add or delete, no editing. Any time, also in a raid, but nothing needs them; they stay on this PC.

A kept card is one clicked to stay open (HelpPointAtQuest, the paragraph before: "Click to keep the card"); only there can a note be added or deleted. Each note shows the day and time it was written; notes are never edited; nothing in Shturmap reads them.

data.name: HelpPrivacy
data.value: Reads screenshot names, the game's logs, tarkov.dev's public data, the extract list in a raid screenshot's top right corner, in a menu screenshot the item cells, for what your quests need and for the desk's prices (matched against every item; which items, how many and where are kept, with a log of the last 50 screenshots read), the item cells of a raid screenshot of your inventory, for what your loot is worth (nothing kept), and the operational tasks on the Tasks screen and a trader's TASKS tab, never their text or rewards (settings turn each off). Reads nothing from the game, sends it nothing. Nothing is sent unless you send a report or allow crash reports; an installed Shturmap asks GitHub for updates. Changes nothing outside its folders unless you tick Delete screenshots after reading.
data.comment: Help: note on what Shturmap reads, sends and changes. "Delete screenshots after reading" is the setting's name (SettingsDeleteScreenshots). "Operational tasks": the daily and weekly tasks on the game's Tasks screen, its OPERATIONAL tab; "a trader's TASKS tab": a trader's screen in the game's TRADERS menu, its TASKS tab, where the daily or weekly selected is read too (owner, 2026-10-25). "The desk": the stash desk, the view beside Plan (PLAN | DESK) that mirrors a stash or GEAR screenshot with each item's price. "A raid screenshot of your inventory": the in-raid glance (owner, 2026-10-19), a plate over the map with what a looted container or body is worth; nothing of it is kept. "A log of the last 50 screenshots read": the readings log (owner, 2026-10-25), a text file per menu screenshot read with what was read on it, kept in Shturmap's data folder for troubleshooting a reading; never sent.

data.name: QuestCardNotes

data.name: SettingsLanguage

data.name: SettingsTextSizeTip

data.comment: Settings: tooltip of each text size step. Windows' own setting and where it is, as Windows names it in the player's language.

data.name: SettingsTextSizeNormal

data.name: SettingsTextSizeLarger
data.comment: Settings, text size: a choice, the text a step larger (×1.25). Upper case, small, like the other choices.

data.name: SettingsTextSizeLargest
data.comment: Settings, text size: a choice, the text largest (×1.5). Upper case, small, like the other choices.

data.name: SettingsReadStash
data.value: Read your stash, gear and tasks from menu screenshots, and loot in a raid
data.comment: Settings: tick box. On, a screenshot taken in the game's menus is read: the item cells (the stash, the GEAR tab's loadout, a case, the key tool) for the items your quests need and, on the stash desk, for what each item is worth; and the game's Tasks screen (its OPERATIONAL tab: the daily and weekly tasks), and a trader's TASKS tab (the daily or weekly selected there; owner, 2026-10-25). In a raid, a screenshot of the inventory screen, the player's own or with a looted container or body, is read for the in-raid glance: a plate over the map with what the loot is worth ("and loot in a raid"; owner, 2026-10-19: the tick's words widened "and in a raid"). "Stash" is the game's word; "gear" is the player's loadout, the game's GEAR tab (Character › GEAR); "loot" the players' word for what is looted. Prices aren't read from the picture (they come from tarkov.dev; the note says so), so the words don't name them. One line of the 480 px panel at the normal text size, or two.

data.name: SettingsForgetMarks
data.comment: Settings: link under the stash tick box that takes back every mark (what Shturmap learned of the stash from screenshots and the game's log) at once, as NOT ANY MORE takes one. Upper case, small.

data.name: SettingsForgetMarksTip
data.value: Takes back every mark, from screenshots and the game's log; the next screenshot marks again
data.comment: Settings: tooltip of FORGET ALL MARKS.

data.name: ItemCardStash
data.comment: An item's or key's card: heading over what Shturmap learned of having the item ("Seen in your stash · 5 Oct"). The game's word for the player's storage. Upper case.

data.name: ItemCardNotAnyMore
data.comment: An item's or key's card, under the STASH line: the button that retracts what Shturmap learned of having the item (it was sold, lost, used up). Upper case, short.

data.name: BringStashNote
data.value: Screenshot your key tool in the game: the keys your quests need get a mark.
data.comment: Under BRING on a map's card, until the first menu screenshot gave a mark: teaches the one thing to do, once. "Key tool" is the game's container for keys.

data.name: CardOperational
data.comment: Heading in a map's card in Plan and in the raid card, over the daily and weekly tasks read from a screenshot of the game's Tasks screen; the game's own name for that tab. Upper case.

data.name: OperationalGlyphTip
data.value: Operational task: a daily or weekly task from your screenshot of the Tasks screen or a trader's TASKS tab
data.comment: Tooltip of the generic symbol beside an operational task whose kind Shturmap doesn't know (a kill, a survival and a hand-over have the quest types' symbols).

data.name: DeskSwitchPlan
data.comment: The rail's head, above the MAP heading: the first of the two words that switch the window's view between the raid planner (this) and the stash desk, each in the title style across half the rail (174 DIP); the one on screen in amber. Capitals; keep it short.

data.name: DeskSwitchDesk
data.comment: The rail's head, above the MAP heading: the second of the two words that switch the window's view, to the stash desk (your stash and gear from a screenshot, each item with its price), each in the title style across half the rail (174 DIP); the one on screen in amber. Capitals; keep it short.

data.name: DeskSwitchPlanTip
data.value: The raid planner: your maps, quests and what to bring
data.comment: Tooltip of PLAN at the rail's head (DeskSwitchPlan).

data.name: DeskSwitchDeskTip
data.value: The desk: your last stash or gear screenshot, each item with its price. Opens by itself when you take one.
data.comment: Tooltip of DESK at the rail's head (DeskSwitchDesk).

data.name: DeskRailHint
data.value: Point at an item for its card. A click copies its flea price; a right-click pins its card here.
data.comment: The rail while the stash desk is up, before an item on it was pointed at: pointing at an item's cell puts its card here; a click on the cell copies its list price to the clipboard; a right-click pins its card in the rail. Muted.

data.name: DeskCompactTip
data.comment: Tooltip of a pinned card shown as one line on the stash desk's rail (its icon, name and figure) while another cell's card stands above it: a click shows the pinned card whole.

data.name: SettingsCopyRule
data.comment: Settings: the row's name for the stash desk's copy rule: what a click on a desk cell copies to the clipboard, the flea's last low matched or 1 to 20 % under or over it; the same rule as the control on the desk's card. Bold, beside the control.

data.name: SettingsCopyRuleNote
data.value: Match, or 1–20% under or over the last low. The desk's card has the same control.
data.comment: Settings: the note under the row SettingsCopyRule, muted: what the rule can be, and that the same control stands on the stash desk's card.

data.name: DeskPinTip
data.value: Pin this card to the rail (or right-click the item)
data.comment: Tooltip and name of the pin at the head of a stash desk's card in the rail: keeps the card in the rail while the pointer goes on to other items; a right-click on the item's cell does the same.

data.name: DeskUnpinTip
data.comment: Tooltip and name of the pin at the head of a stash desk's card pinned in the rail: takes the card out of the rail.

data.name: HelpDesk
data.value: The desk (DESK, at the top of the left column): your last stash or gear screenshot, each item priced; point at an item for its card, click it to copy its flea price (the card sets how), right-click it to pin its card.
data.comment: Help: paragraph on the stash desk, the view beside Plan that mirrors a stash or GEAR screenshot with each item's price: its card, the click that copies a list price, the right-click that pins the card. One sentence.
